Static Contiguous Image-Based Partitioning is a parallel volume rendering strategy that divides the final image plane into contiguous blocks (tiles) and assigns each block to a specific processor, which then executes the complete rendering pipeline for that region [S1][S3, unofficial].

The claim describes 'Static Contiguous Image-Based Partitioning' as a strategy where the image plane is divided into contiguous blocks (tiles) and each processor executes the complete rendering pipeline for its assigned region. Source [S1] explicitly defines the 'Image Order' approach where 'pixels are partitioned among processors into groups called tiles' and 'each processor generates the portion of the image corresponding to its tile'. Source [S3] describes 'Sort-first' systems (which follow an image order distribution approach) where 'The final image is split into disjoint tiles and distributed across the rendering processors. Every processor effectively applies the complete pipeline to their piece of work.' The term 'Static' in the claim likely refers to the fixed assignment of tiles to processors for the duration of the rendering task (as opposed to dynamic load balancing techniques mentioned in the sources as alternatives or enhancements), and 'Contiguous' refers to the 'groups of consecutive pixels' mentioned in S1. Since the core mechanism described in the claim (image partitioning into tiles, full pipeline execution per tile) is fully supported by the evidence in both sources, the verdict is supported.
